extracted.intended_audience: U.S. patent examiners and patent applicants/attorneys/agents
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and practices for computing, extending, resetting, and reacting to reply periods in U.S. patent prosecution (37 CFR 1.7, 1.8, 1.136, 1.135, 1.137, 1.138 etc.), including abandonment and petitions to reset.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction between specified time and shortened statutory period
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners and applicants should not lose sight of the distinction between a specified time for a particular action and a shortened statutory period for reply under 35 U.S.C. 133.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to take action within a specified time generally results in loss of rights as to that particular matter (e.g., disclaiming subject matter), whereas failure to reply within a shortened statutory period under 35 U.S.C. 133 results in abandonment of the entire application (abandonment is not appealable; petition to revive may be granted if delay was unavoidable or unintentional under 37 CFR 1.137).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of late reply to shortened statutory period
rubrics_metrics.description: A reply one day late in an application carrying a shortened statutory period under 35 U.S.C. 133 results in abandonment regardless of excuse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner discretion to excuse small delays applies to specified times, but not to shortened statutory periods; extensions under 37 CFR 1.136 may be available only within statutory limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specified times/time limits are not shortened statutory periods
rubrics_metrics.description: A specified time or time limit set by the Office is not a shortened statutory period under 35 U.S.C. 133.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accordingly the Office may specify a time for action of less than the 30 day minimum in 35 U.S.C. 133, and such periods are generally extendable under 37 CFR 1.136 (see MPEP § 103).

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of extensions under 37 CFR 1.136(a)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicant is required to reply within a nonstatutory or shortened statutory time period, applicant may extend the time for reply up to the earlier of the expiration of any maximum period set by statute or five months after the time period set for reply, if a petition for an extension of time and the fee set in § 1.17(a) are filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions where 1.136(a) is not available include (i) applicant notified otherwise in an Office action; (ii) reply is a reply brief under §1.193(b); (iii) reply is request for oral hearing under §1.194(b); (iv) reply to Board decisions under §§1.196/1.197/1.304; (v) application involved in an interference under §1.611. The date the petition and fee are filed determines the extension period and fee amount; reply must be filed prior to expiration to avoid abandonment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructive petition/fee authorizations under 37 CFR 1.136(a)(3)
rubrics_metrics.description: A written request may authorize treating any concurrent or future reply requiring a petition for extension under 1.136(a) as incorporating such a petition; authorization to charge fees or submission of the fee will be treated as a constructive petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This 'safety net' avoids loss of rights where a petition was inadvertently omitted. Office strongly recommends including a written petition with a reply to avoid processing delays. Office practice may construe an insufficiently-phrased petition as requesting the necessary period when a fee authorization/deposit account is present (example provided).

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensions for cause under 37 CFR 1.136(b)
rubrics_metrics.description: When a reply cannot be filed within the time period and the provisions of 1.136(a) are not available, the period for reply will be extended only for sufficient cause and for a reasonable time specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests under 1.136(b) must be filed on or before the day the reply is due; mere filing does not effect an extension; the request must state a reason; extensions decided by the Group Director; no extension may operate to extend past the maximum statutory period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Situations where extensions under 1.136 are not allowed
rubrics_metrics.description: Extensions of time with payment of a fee pursuant to 1.136 are possible in reply to most Office actions, but there are exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions include: all extensions in reexamination proceedings (see 1.550(c)); all extensions during an interference proceeding (except preparatory interference where a claim is suggested); situations where Office action states 1.136(a) is not applicable (e.g., litigation-related reissue applications); and limited instances where applicant is given a specified time limit to take certain actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee computation and small entity reduction for extension fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Fees for extensions of time are set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(a) and are cumulative; small entities receive a 50% reduction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant paid a 1-month extension fee and later needs an additional month, the proper fee is the amount for a 2-month extension less the amount previously paid (i.e., cumulative calculation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing petition and fee timing rules under 1.136(a)(2)
rubrics_metrics.description: The date on which the petition and fee are filed is the date for determining the period of extension and corresponding fee; a reply must be filed prior to expiration of the period of extension to avoid abandonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A petition under 1.136(a) need not be accompanied by a reply; but if extension is obtained solely for copendency and no reply is filed, the application will become abandoned upon expiration of the so-extended period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure when reply filed after set period without petition/fee
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a reply is filed after the set period with no petition or fee, the reply will not be accepted as timely until the petition (or constructive petition) and the appropriate fee are submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: action sets 3-month period, applicant replies in 4th month with petition for 1-month extension only — reply is not acceptable until correct fee is filed; if fee not filed until 5th month, an additional fee for the 2nd month extension is required to render reply timely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental reply rule
rubrics_metrics.description: An extension under 1.136 is not necessary when submitting a supplemental reply to an Office action if a complete first reply was timely filed in reply to the Office action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Group Director handling and form procedure for 1.136(b) requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests for extension under 1.136(b) must be filed on or before the due date and are to be decided by the Group Director; duplicate filings with stamped self-addressed envelope will be returned with notation of action taken.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When granted/denied, Office will indicate action on original and return copy; notation on original signed by person granting/denying extension; extent of partial grants indicated; if denied, reasons are indicated or formal decision letter sent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computation of due date when extension granted
rubrics_metrics.description: If the request for extension is granted, the due date is computed from the date stamped or printed on the Office action (the remailing or acknowledged date), not the original due date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 3-month shortened statutory period dated Nov 30 is due Feb 28; if extended one month, reply due Mar 30 (not Mar 28).

rubrics_metrics.name: Special final rejection rule for first replies and advisory actions
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicant initially replies within 2 months from the mailing of any final rejection setting a 3-month shortened statutory period and the Office does not mail an advisory action until after the end of the 3-month period, the period for reply for purposes of determining any extension fee will be the date the advisory action is mailed, but in no event later than 6 months from the date of final rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners must include specified language in each final rejection notifying applicants of this rule. Example explanatory language is provided in the text; applies only to a first reply to a final rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Issue fee non-extendability and informalities after allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: The statutory (nonextendable) time period for payment of the issue fee is 3 months from the date of the Notice of Allowance (35 U.S.C. 151).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If informality corrections (drawings, declarations) are outstanding at allowance, PTOL-37 will notify applicant; extensions under 1.136(a) are available to correct informalities, but the issue fee must still be paid within 3 months.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of two different reply periods running
rubrics_metrics.description: When two different periods for reply are running against an application, the running of the first period is not suspended or affected by an ex parte limited time action or an appeal therefrom (with certain exceptions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In copying patent claims where copied claims are rejected and other claims have an unanswered rejection, the controlling date is the date of the last unanswered Office action on the claims other than the copied patent claims (see Ex parte Milton and MPEP §2305.02).

rubrics_metrics.name: Weekend/holiday expiration rule
rubrics_metrics.description: When the last day for taking action or paying a fee falls on Saturday, Sunday, or a Federal holiday within the District of Columbia, the action may be taken, or the fee paid, on the next succeeding day which is not Saturday, Sunday, or a Federal holiday (35 U.S.C. 21; 37 CFR 1.7).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Federal holidays list provided; when a Federal holiday falls on a Saturday the preceding Friday is considered a Federal holiday; if an amendment is filed on the succeeding business day the file is endorsed with the date of receipt and indication of the holiday/weekend.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restart/restart of reply period for defective Office action (incorrect citation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the citation of a reference is incorrect or an Office action contains some other defect and this error is called to the Office's attention within 1 month of the mail date, the Office will restart the previously set period for reply to run from the date the error is corrected if requested by applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If called to the Office's attention within the reply period but more than 1 month after mailing, the Office will set a new period substantially equal to the time remaining (new period must be at least 1 month). If the error is called to attention after expiration of the period, the period will not be restarted and an appropriate extension fee is required. See MPEP §707.05(g) for record correction procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remailing and supplementary action reset rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Where it becomes necessary to remail any action, the action should be redated; remailing date establishes the beginning of the period for reply. A supplementary action after a rejection explaining references or reasons more fully establishes a new date from which the statutory period runs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Ex parte Gourtoff and related MPEP sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition to reset period due to late receipt (mail delay) criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: The PTO will grant a petition to restart the previously set period for reply to run from the date of receipt at the correspondence address when criteria are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criteria: (A) petition filed within 2 weeks of date of receipt at correspondence address; (B) a substantial portion of the set reply period had elapsed on date of receipt (e.g., at least 1 month of a 2- or 3-month reply period); (C) petition includes evidence of receipt date (e.g., copy of PTO action stamped with receipt date or envelope) and a statement explaining how the evidence establishes receipt date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition to reset period due to postmark later than mail date criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: The PTO will grant a petition to restart the previously set period to run from the postmark date on the mailing envelope when criteria are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criteria: (A) petition filed within 2 weeks of receipt; (B) the reply period was for payment of the issue fee or the period set was 1 month/30 days; (C) petition includes evidence of receipt and a copy of the envelope showing the postmark date and a statement of receipt date. 37 CFR 1.8 and 1.10 apply regarding filing within 2 weeks. The showings may be insufficient if circumstances suggest delay after receipt rather than in the mail or PTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abandonment for failure to reply (37 CFR 1.135) and express abandonment (37 CFR 1.138)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicant fails to reply within the time periods provided under §§1.134 and 1.136, the application becomes abandoned unless an Office action indicates otherwise. An application may also be expressly abandoned by filing a written declaration of abandonment signed by applicant or attorney/agent of record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prosecution to save from abandonment must include a complete and proper reply; admission or refusal of amendments after final rejection will not save the application from abandonment. Express abandonment becomes effective when an appropriate Office official recognizes it; express abandonment may be recognized as of a different date if so specified (e.g., conditional abandonment upon filing of a continuing application). Special care required when attorney/agent signs express abandonment to ensure it reflects applicant's desires; divisional applications should be reviewed before filing to decide if prior application should be abandoned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavits filed after final rejection and extension of time to submit affidavits
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants often request extensions to submit affidavits after final rejection; granting such an extension is without prejudice to the examiner's right to question why affidavit was not earlier presented and the examiner may deny entry if the showing is insufficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grant of extension merely keeps the case from becoming abandoned and allows applicant opportunity to present the affidavit or take other action. Affidavits submitted after final rejection are treated as amendments submitted after final rejection; admission or refusal of such affidavit will not, by itself, save the application from abandonment (In re Affidavit Filed After Final Rejection, 152 USPQ 292).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of form paragraph 7.98 when reply is late but extension possible
rubrics_metrics.description: Form Paragraph 7.98 may be used where a reply is filed late but an extension of time under 37 CFR 1.136(a) is possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paragraph text alerts applicant that reply was received after expiration and that application will become abandoned unless applicant obtains extension under 37 CFR 1.136(a). Do not use in reexamination or litigation-related reissue applications where 1.136(a) does not apply.
